payload.rationale: I estimate an 86% chance that the BEA’s Q3 2026 advance estimate reports annualized real GDP growth above 2.0%. Because settlement uses the published one-decimal figure, 2.1% or higher qualifies; 2.0% does not. The strongest supplied evidence is the Atlanta Fed’s September 17 GDPNow estimate of 5.1%, up from 4.4% on September 10 and comfortably above the threshold. That directly targets the relevant quarter and growth measure, although it is not the BEA release. Q1 growth of 2.1% and Q2 second-estimate growth of 1.5% provide a weaker prior of moderate expansion. The FOMC’s 2.3% Q4/Q4 projection offers broad context, not a directly comparable Q3 forecast. My judgment gives substantial weight to GDPNow while allowing for meaningful forecast error and remaining data releases. The strongest reason this probability could be too high is that subsequent source data, especially volatile inventory and trade contributions, could sharply reduce the nowcast or produce a weaker advance estimate. The strongest reason it could be too low is that a late-quarter nowcast already 3.1 percentage points above the threshold may be sufficiently informative that falling to 2.0% or below requires an unusually large downside miss.
limitations: No browsing or independent verification; the estimate relies on the supplied evidence available at the cutoff.
No historical GDPNow error distribution was supplied or fitted, so the probability is judgmental rather than statistically calibrated.
Detailed Q3 expenditure components and a broader set of independent forecasts are unavailable.
Settlement concerns the BEA advance estimate and its published rounding, not subsequent GDP revisions.
